report.summary: Both previous criticals are fixed and verified (the CA pointer can no longer be NULL, mqtt_load_config() runs again before the STA/AP decision, and the pinned CA is reachable and applied with a client restart); the only remaining items are the owner-accepted TLS name-check skip plus two info-level notes.

notes: Factory reset remains a 10 s hold of the single front button rather than the spec's SET+MODE combination — a deviation the writer documented as unavoidable on this board; not a regression.

TLS for the broker skips the certificate name check (skip_cert_common_name_check) for every mqtts/ssl/:8883 URI, kept deliberately at the product owner's request; the chain is still verified and a pinned CA can now be supplied from the settings page.
A freshly flashed panel defaults to mqtts://homeassistant.gdenu.fi:8123 (owner's request) and needs only Wi-Fi to reach it.
The settings form's CA field is never pre-filled (the stored PEM is not echoed) and cannot be cleared from the page; the 4 KB fixed CA buffer is truncation-safe.
No new defects found in this round; both previous criticals are fixed at the root.

findings.description: For every TLS broker URI the client runs with skip_cert_common_name_check = true (the esp-mqtt header documents this as enabling MITM). Kept deliberately at the product owner's request; the chain is still verified and a pinned CA is now reachable from the settings page.
findings.evidence: app_mqtt.cpp:199-203 (skip_cert_common_name_check for every mqtts/ssl/:8883 URI, certificate = s_ca_pem when set); heating_web.cpp:223-225 page text; heating_web.cpp:318-333 app_mqtt_set_broker_ca(form_get("ca")).
findings.failureScenario: Anyone on the path presenting any certificate from a public CA is accepted as the broker, because the name is not matched; a pinned CA (now enterable on the settings page) removes that exposure but is optional and not persisted.
findings.suggestedChange: Persist the CA in NVS so a pinned household stays pinned across reboots, and consider offering a strict (name-checked) mode for brokers whose certificate actually matches the dialled host.

findings.description: The factory reset is a 10 s hold of the single front button (adc_button_group handles[0]) rather than the spec's 'SET and MODE together for 10 s'. Documented by the writer as unobservable on this board; not a regression, and a tap can no longer schedule it.
findings.evidence: app_logic.cpp:373-376 (COMBO_ARM_MS registered on handles[0]); app_logic.cpp:247-258 on_set_arm; spec.json factoryReset.trigger.
findings.failureScenario: A user holding the front button for 10 s wipes Wi-Fi, broker and room topics with no second button confirming the intent.
findings.suggestedChange: Either accept and document the deviation in the product description, or gate the wipe behind a combination (e.g. with the volume key) if the button device can report it.

findings.description: The CA field is never pre-filled (the stored PEM is deliberately not echoed) and an empty submission cannot clear it, so a pinned CA can be replaced but not removed from the page.
findings.evidence: heating_web.cpp:223-225 (empty <textarea name="ca">); heating_web.cpp:321-333 (`if (form_get("apass")[0] || form_get("ca")[0]) … if (form_get("ca")[0]) app_mqtt_set_broker_ca(...)`).
findings.failureScenario: After pinning a CA the user moves the panel to a broker that needs the built-in pack: the stored CA stays in s_ca_buf until the next reboot (it is not in NVS), varying behaviour between a live edit and a power cycle.
findings.suggestedChange: Accept an explicit sentinel (e.g. '-') to clear the CA, as the username/password flow already does in mqtt-setup.
